DECISIONS — Platform Design Records (ADRs)

Difference from WORKFLOW_IMPROVEMENTS.md: this file records design decisions (why we chose X over Y). WORKFLOW_IMPROVEMENTS.md records corrections (what was wrong and how it was fixed).

The normative PT-BR version is the full record (the source of truth); this English translation is faithful to it.

ADR-001 - Layered Architecture: Primary → Subagent → Skill

  • Date: 2026-04-22
  • Decider: Operator
  • Status: Accepted
  • Context: OpenCode supports primary agents, subagents and skills. We needed an architecture that allowed: (1) clear delegation of responsibilities, (2) granular permissions, (3) knowledge reuse, (4) flexible orchestration.
  • Decision: We adopted the Primary Agent → Subagent → Skill hierarchy:
    • Primary Agent (the GOLMET triad: gm-req, gm-doc, gm-dev): the active persona of the session, broad permissions, routes to subagents.
    • Subagent (@gm-intake-orchestrator, @gm-figma-orchestrator, etc.): domain orchestrator, scoped permissions, invokes skills of its domain.
    • Skill (gm-requirements, gm-data-model, etc.): reference knowledge, executable standalone, stateless.
  • Alternatives considered:
    • Skills directly from the primary: simpler, but without granular permissions and without separation of responsibilities.
    • Subagents without skills: self-contained subagents, but with duplicated knowledge and hard to maintain.
    • Microservices: overkill for the context (local config, not deployed).
  • Consequences:
    • ✓ Granular permissions per subagent (least privilege)
    • ✓ Skill reuse across subagents (e.g. gm-task-spec accessed by @gm-quality-orchestrator and @gm-azure-orchestrator)
    • ✓ Clear separation between orchestration (subagent) and execution (skill)
    • ✗ Initial complexity (3 layers to understand)
    • ✗ Need to keep ARCHITECTURE.md in sync

ADR-002 - Golmet- Prefix on All Components

  • Date: 2026-04-22
  • Decider: Operator
  • Status: Accepted
  • Context: OpenCode allows free naming for skills and subagents. We needed a naming convention that: (1) identified GOLMET components instantly, (2) avoided conflicts with skills from other workflows, (3) made searches and references easy.
  • Decision: Every GOLMET skill and subagent uses the Golmet- prefix (e.g. gm-requirements, @gm-intake-orchestrator). Primary agents follow the GOLMET triad (gm-req, gm-doc, gm-dev). External skills may keep their own prefix (organization project skills).
  • Alternatives considered:
    • opencode- prefix: too generic, does not identify the domain.
    • No prefix: conflicts with skills from other workflows.
    • Domain prefixes (gm-intake-, gm-azure-): too many prefixes, unnecessary complexity.
  • Consequences:
    • ✓ Instant identification of GOLMET components
    • ✓ No conflicts with other workflows
    • ✓ Easy searches (grep Golmet-)
    • ✗ Slightly longer names
    • ✗ Requires consistency (already broken once - IMP-008)

ADR-003 - Stable and Immutable IDs (RN-XXX, PEND-XXX)

  • Date: 2026-04-22
  • Decider: Operator
  • Status: Accepted
  • Context: Requirements change over time. We needed a traceability mechanism that: (1) allowed referencing a requirement across multiple documents, (2) did not break references when the requirement was renamed, (3) supported incremental merge.
  • Decision: IDs are assigned once and never renumbered:
    • RN-XXX for business rules (e.g. RN-001)
    • PEND-XXX for clarification pending items (e.g. PEND-001)
    • Removed IDs get a [removed] tag but keep the number (IMP-008)
  • Alternatives considered:
    • Timestamp-based IDs: hard to remember, not human-readable.
    • Renumberable IDs: break references in downstream documents.
    • UUIDs: overkill, hard to work with manually.
  • Consequences:
    • ✓ Stable references across documents
    • ✓ Incremental merge works without numbering conflicts
    • ✓ Easy to remember and reference in conversations
    • ✗ Gaps in numbering (removed IDs leave "holes")
    • ✗ Need to document the [removed] tag for IDs with external relevance

ADR-004 - Document DAG with Integrity Validation

  • Date: 2026-04-22
  • Decider: Operator
  • Status: Accepted
  • Context: Requirements and architecture documents reference each other. We needed: (1) a clear dependency order, (2) detection of orphan or stale artifacts, (3) controlled change propagation.
  • Decision: Each module follows a DAG (Directed Acyclic Graph):
    PROJECT_CHARTER → REQUIREMENTS → [DATA_MODEL, API_CONTRACTS, UI_SPEC, ARCHITECTURE, GLOSSARIES, ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA] → [TEST_STRATEGY, TRACEABILITY, VALIDATION_REPORT, TASKS]
    Validation is done by gm-validate; propagation by @gm-cr-propagation-guard.
  • Alternatives considered: Independent documents: no traceability, inevitable drift. Relational database: overkill for markdown, loses Git versioning. Wikis with links: no automatic validation, depends on human discipline.
  • Consequences:
    • ✓ Full traceability (RN → downstream artifact)
    • ✓ Automatic drift detection (PROPAGATION_STATUS.md)
    • ✓ Integrity validation (VALIDATION_REPORT.md)
    • ✗ DAG complexity (7+ documents per module)
    • ✗ Need to run gm-validate periodically

ADR-005 - Manual Self-Update (No Hook/Plugin)

  • Date: 2026-08-14
  • Decider: Operator
  • Status: Accepted
  • Context: The GOLMET config is a git repo (<config-repo>). We needed a mechanism to update it without destroying local work.
  • Decision: Self-update is manual and controlled via the gm-self-update skill:
    • Checks the working tree before pull (if dirty, ABORTS)
    • Uses git pull --ff-only (never automatic merge)
    • Warns to restart OpenCode (config is not hot-reloaded)
  • Alternatives considered and rejected:
    • Hook/plugin auto-pull on session.created: pull does not apply at session start (config already loaded), may silently merge/overwrite WIP, plugins are not versioned.
    • Cron job: risky to overwrite local work, implementation complexity.
    • File watch: OpenCode does not support hot-reload of config.
  • Consequences:
    • ✓ Never destroys local work (working tree lock)
    • ✓ Full operator control (decides when to update)
    • ✓ Simple to implement (pure skill, no hooks)
    • ✗ Requires manual action (forgetting = stale config)
    • ✗ Requires OpenCode restart after update

ADR-006 - Publishing via Git Push (No CI/CD)

  • Date: 2026-08-18
  • Decider: Operator
  • Status: Accepted
  • Context: Improvements applied by @gm-workflow-improver and @gm-workflow-builder were stuck on the local machine. We needed a publishing mechanism.
  • Decision: Publishing via the gm-self-publish skill:
    • Atomic commit per theme (Conventional Commits)
    • pull --ff-only before push (never force)
    • Confirmation gate (never blind commit)
    • Versioning scope: agents/Golmet-*.md, skills/Golmet-*/SKILL.md, ARCHITECTURE-*.md, WORKFLOW_IMPROVEMENTS.md
  • Alternatives considered and rejected:
    • CI/CD (Azure Pipelines): too complex for a local config, maintenance overhead.
    • Automatic sync: risky (may publish incomplete work).
    • Manual (git add/commit/push): no safety gates, error-prone.
  • Consequences:
    • ✓ Safe publishing with confirmation gates
    • ✓ Clean history (atomic commits)
    • ✓ Compatible with gm-self-update (same repo, same branch)
    • ✗ Requires manual action (same cost as update)
    • ✗ No code review (direct push to master)

ADR-007 - Broad Permission for Primary Agents

  • Date: 2026-04-22
  • Decider: Operator
  • Status: Accepted (with caveats)
  • Context: OpenCode does not support permission delegation from primary to subagent at invocation time. Primary agents need to coordinate subagents with different permissions.
  • Decision: Primary agents (the GOLMET triad: gm-req, gm-doc, gm-dev) have broad permissions (read/write/edit/bash/webfetch). Subagents have scoped permissions (least privilege). The primary's blast-radius is accepted as controlled risk.
  • Alternatives considered:
    • Scoped permission on the primary: OpenCode does not support delegation at invocation time.
    • Self-contained subagents: loss of centralized orchestration.
    • Multi-primary: unnecessary complexity for the context.
  • Consequences:
    • ✓ Flexible orchestration (primary coordinates any subagent)
    • ✓ Works with the current OpenCode API
    • ✗ Elevated blast-radius (primary can edit anything)
    • ✗ Trust in the primary's behavior (mitigated by conventions)

ADR-008 - Self-Contained vs. Orchestrated

  • Date: 2026-08-14
  • Decider: Operator
  • Status: Accepted
  • Context: Some subagents only need to read artifacts and produce output (without invoking skills). Others need to orchestrate multiple skills.
  • Decision: Two kinds of subagent:
    • Self-contained (@gm-next, @gm-progress, @gm-cr-propagation-guard): read artifacts directly, do not invoke skills, are lightweight.
    • Orchestrated (@gm-intake-orchestrator, @gm-azure-orchestrator, etc.): invoke skills of their domain, have routing logic.
  • Alternatives considered: All orchestrated: unnecessary overhead for simple subagents. All self-contained: loss of skill reuse.
  • Consequences:
    • ✓ Efficiency (self-contained are fast)
    • ✓ Skill reuse (orchestrated share knowledge)
    • ✓ Flexibility (each kind for its use case)
    • ✗ Two patterns to understand
    • ✗ Need to classify correctly when creating new subagents

ADR-009 - WORKFLOW_IMPROVEMENTS.md as Immutable Log

  • Date: 2026-08-13
  • Decider: Operator
  • Status: Accepted
  • Context: Workflow improvements needed traceability (what changed, why it changed, when it changed).
  • Decision: WORKFLOW_IMPROVEMENTS.md is an immutable log:
    • Each entry is incremental (never delete previous entries)
    • Standardized format: Date, Target, Problem, Root cause, Fix, Files, Status
    • Numbered entries (IMP-001, IMP-002, ...)
  • Alternatives considered: Traditional changelog (CHANGELOG.md): mixes features with fixes, hard to filter. Git log: has no "why" context, only "what". Wiki: no structure, hard to query programmatically.
  • Consequences:
    • ✓ Complete and immutable history
    • ✓ Standardized format (easy to query)
    • ✓ "Why" context preserved
    • ✗ File grows indefinitely (acceptable for the current volume)
    • ✗ Requires discipline to register (not automatic)

ADR-010 - Task Title Convention [<repo>] <description>

  • Date: 2026-08-18
  • Decider: Operator (based on team practice)
  • Status: Accepted
  • Context: Tasks needed a consistent format that: (1) identified the target repository, (2) was human-readable, (3) supported domain classification.
  • Decision: Task title follows the pattern [{prefix}] [<repo>] <description>:
    • [Database] for DDL/DML
    • [DevOps] for pipelines/deploy
    • {repo} is required (e.g. [Traceability.API])
    • One task = one repository/scope
  • Alternatives considered: Free title: inconsistent, hard to filter. Business-area prefix: [NF]- is unreadable, does not identify the repo. Multiple repos in the same task: violates the granularity principle.
  • Consequences:
    • ✓ Visual consistency and filtering
    • ✓ Traceability (repo identified in the title)
    • ✓ Compatible with existing team practice
    • ✗ Longer titles
    • ✗ Requires discipline (one task = one repo)

ADR-011 - Review Gate: TASKS.md Before Azure

  • Date: 2026-08-18
  • Decider: Operator
  • Status: Accepted
  • Context: Tasks were being created in Azure DevOps without prior review, generating duplicated and inconsistent work.
  • Decision: Mandatory gate:
    1. gm-task-spec generates TASKS.md (reviewable markdown)
    2. Operator reviews and confirms (via question)
    3. @gm-azure-orchestrator only then creates work items in AzDO
  • Alternatives considered: Direct creation: fast, but without review (already generated duplicates). Automatic review: impossible without human context. Double confirmation: unnecessary overhead.
  • Consequences:
    • ✓ Eliminates accidental creation of duplicate tasks
    • ✓ Allows human review before writing
    • ✓ Materializes the work in auditable markdown
    • ✗ One extra step (gate)
    • ✗ Requires the module to have TASKS.md before creating in AzDO

ADR-012 - Duplicate Detection Before Creating Tasks

  • Date: 2026-09-03
  • Decider: Operator
  • Status: Accepted
  • Context: Even with the review gate, duplicate tasks were created when the operator re-ran a PBI that already had child tasks.
  • Decision: Mandatory duplicate gate:
    1. Read PBI with expand: "Relations" to get existing child tasks
    2. Compare existing task titles with the ones in TASKS.md
    3. Exact match → skip creation (inform the operator)
    4. Approximate match → ask the operator
    5. Fail-open if MCP fails (does not block on infrastructure error)
  • Alternatives considered: Manual verification: error-prone, relies on memory. ID as key: titles change, IDs are more stable but less readable. No check: accept duplicates (unacceptable).
  • Consequences:
    • ✓ Eliminates 100% of accidental duplicates
    • ✓ Transparency (operator is informed)
    • ✓ Fail-open (does not block on infrastructure error)
    • ✗ Extra call to AzDO (expand: Relations)
    • ✗ Approximate match may generate false positives

ADR-013 - Standard Audit Columns

  • Date: 2026-09-03
  • Decider: Operator
  • Status: Accepted
  • Context: New tables were being created without the standard audit columns, generating inconsistency with the legacy and making migration harder.
  • Decision: Every new table must include the audit columns defined in CONSTITUTION.md (e.g. 6 columns with the CTR_ prefix). Names always in UPPER CASE.
  • Alternatives considered: camelCase columns (dataHora, createdAt): inconsistent with the legacy, breaks migration. No audit columns: loss of traceability of who created/updated. Trigger-based audit: complex, performance overhead.
  • Consequences:
    • ✓ Create/update traceability
    • ✓ Simplified migration (legacy uses the same pattern)
    • ✗ Long names (e.g. 6 columns with the CTR_ prefix)
    • ✗ Requires discipline in every DDL task

ADR-014 - Business Glossary 100% in Portuguese

  • Date: 2026-08-20
  • Decider: Operator
  • Status: Accepted
  • Context: The business glossary was being generated with English terms in parentheses, making it hard for non-technical stakeholders to understand.
  • Decision: BUSINESS_GLOSSARY.md is 100% in Portuguese:
    • Titles in Portuguese (e.g. ## Vacinação)
    • Parentheses only for acronyms/expansions in Portuguese (e.g. ## GTA (Guia de Trânsito Animal))
    • Concepts that only exist in English → translate the title and explain in the definition
  • Alternatives considered: Bilingual (## Vacinação (Vaccination)): confusing for non-technical stakeholders, pollutes the document. Pure English: inaccessible to business stakeholders. Portuguese with a separate technical glossary: ?, hard to maintain.
  • Consequences:
    • ✓ Accessible to non-technical stakeholders
    • ✓ Consistent with the project's PT-BR convention
    • ✓ Acronyms preserved (GTA, PNIB, etc.)
    • ✗ Technical terms may lose precision in translation
    • ✗ Requires careful translation

ADR-015 - Page Breaks in Documents

  • Date: 2026-08-26
  • Decider: Operator
  • Status: Accepted
  • Context: Documents converted to PDF appeared as running text without page breaks.
  • Decision: Insert <div style="page-break-before: always;"></div> before the main sections in the factory-external templates.
  • Alternatives considered: Separate CSS: depends on the PDF converter, not portable. Pure Markdown: does not support page breaks natively. Converter configuration: varies by tool, not robust.
  • Consequences:
    • ✓ PDFs with professional layout
    • ✓ Compatible with most PDF converters
    • ✓ Does not affect content (formatting only)
    • ✗ Inline HTML in markdown (a bit "dirty")
    • ✗ May break in converters that do not support HTML

ADR-016 - Variable Groups in the <repo>-<env> Pattern

  • Date: 2026-08-28
  • Decider: Operator
  • Status: Accepted
  • Context: CI/CD Variable Groups were being named inconsistently, making it hard to identify the repository and environment.
  • Decision: Variable Groups follow the <repo>-<env> pattern:
    • <name>.API-DES (development)
    • <name>.API-HML (staging)
    • <name>.API-PRO (production)
  • Alternatives considered: Free name: inconsistent, hard to filter. Project prefix: redundant (the repo already identifies the project). No environment: does not allow per-environment configuration.
  • Consequences:
    • ✓ Consistency and easy filtering
    • ✓ Clear repo + environment identification
    • ✓ Compatible with Helm pipelines
    • ✗ Longer names
    • ✗ Requires discipline at creation

ADR-017 - The GOLMET Triad of Primary Agents (gm-req, gm-doc, gm-dev)

  • Date: 2026-09-17
  • Decider: Operator /
  • Status: Accepted
  • Context: The gm-build primary accumulated responsibilities of business discovery (forward) and legacy code documentation (reverse). The user proposed aligning each letter of the GOLMET acronym directly to a specialized Primary Agent:
    • R → gm-req (Requirements)
    • D → gm-doc (Documentation)
    • D → gm-dev (Development)
  • Decision: We replaced gm-build with the GOLMET triad:
    • gm-req: focused on discovery with client/PO, clarification of ambiguities, generation of REQUIREMENTS.md, scope alignment and Change Requests.
    • gm-doc: focused on multi-repo code reverse engineering (IMP-013), isolated technical inspection via @gm-reverse-orchestrator with DDD shielding and evidence, and materialization of specs/.
    • gm-dev: focused on code implementation and green tests from approved tasks.
  • Alternatives considered:
    • Keep gm-build with sub-modes: cognitive overload and mixing postures (discovery vs. archaeology).
    • gm-retro instead of gm-doc: less mnemonic, breaks the acronym symmetry.
  • Consequences:
    • ✓ Absolute cognitive clarity for the operator (Tab between R, D and D)
    • ✓ Context isolation in gm-doc via @gm-reverse-orchestrator
    • ✓ Clear separation between business elicitation and code archaeology

ADR-018 - The GOLMET Quadri: Expansion with the gm-devops Primary

  • Date: 2026-10-18
  • Decider: Operator /
  • Status: Accepted
  • Context: ADR-017 registered the Triad (gm-req, gm-doc, gm-dev). The DevOps domain (VPS setup, deploy pipeline, troubleshooting and observability — IMP-101) grew without its own primary, and the registry/ARCHITECTURE already treated the workflow as "Quadri" while the README, glossary and footers said "Triad" — documentation diverging from the real state. The same review (IMP-106) found duplicate numbering in ADR-014 (Glossary → Triad); the Triad entry was renumbered to ADR-017.
  • Decision: Formalize the GOLMET Quadri: gm-req, gm-doc, gm-dev and gm-devops. The gm-devops is a primary with broad permission in the same pattern as the original Triad, delegating to @gm-devops-orchestrator. Previous ADRs citing "Triad" remain immutable as historical record; from this entry on, the convention is "GOLMET Quadri".
  • Alternatives considered:
    • Keep the Triad and route DevOps through gm-dev: mixes implementation with infrastructure and perpetuates the documentation divergence.
    • A fifth primary for integrations (GitHub/Figma): integration domains are well served by orchestrator subagents.
  • Consequences:
    • ✓ Documentation aligned to the real registry state (ACHIEVEMENT of the architectural analysis IMP-106)
    • ✓ Onboarding and routing between primaries now include the DevOps route
    • ✗ Historical references to the Triad require contextual reading (ADR-017 is the origin)
    • Errata (2026-10-18): the clause "broad permission in the same pattern as the original Triad" is imprecise for gm-devops — it keeps the IMP-103 scope (edit/write: deny, guided mode where the operator executes on the VPS; see PERMISSIONS.md, Primary agents, status "adjusted"). The decision to formalize the Quadri remains unchanged.

ADR-019 - Knowledge Graph Engine in Go (CLI golmet graph + gm_graph tool)

  • Date: 2026-11-20
  • Decider: Operator (Victor Souza)
  • Status: Accepted
  • Context: The gm-knowledge-graph skill was designed around an external deterministic script (scripts/build-knowledge-graph.mjs) executed via Node by the agentic runtime (IMP-148, Node ≥ 18). The component was born a GHOST (IMP-008: SKILL.md documenting a script that did not exist — the skill aborted at step 2), was implemented in Node in the previous cycle and validated with a 38-check fixture with byte-for-byte parity against the session palliative (183 nodes · 398 edges). Porting the engine into the binary removes the kit's last external runtime dependency for deterministic work and aligns the command with established patterns (validate/doctor/lint).
  • Decision: Port the COMPLETE engine (T1-T5 parsers, pruning, sanitation, content selector, 3 emitters) to Go inside the binary, with three surfaces:
    • CLI golmet graph — flags --config-root --packs-root --projects-root --out --pack --scope --max-nodes --from-json --what --json; same artifact contract (graph.json, knowledge-graph.html, knowledge-graph.md); strict ONLY on the registry (exit 1); missing T1-T4 = warning + partial graph; all-or-nothing output; no network; self-contained HTML with the template embedded in the binary.
    • MCP tool gm_graph (15th tool) — thin wrapper over the internal Go function (same pattern as gm_validate/gm_doctor); read-only on sources; NO confirm (only writes the 3 artifacts to the destination).
    • Skill gm-knowledge-graph — step 2 now runs golmet graph (or gm_graph); noise judgment (step 3) remains AGENTIC.
    • Architecture principle (normative record): deterministic work lives in the CLI; organization knowledge lives in the PACK (read-only data, no logic); judgment lives in the RUNTIME (agentic skill).
    • Content selector --what (tool intent: "visual graph of the Golmet ecosystem" — the Golmet structure itself, the pack, the generated docs, or all three at once):
what Stores Content
workflow T5 registry (primaries, subagents, domains, skills), AGENTS.md, fundado_em
pack T1+T2+T3 knowledge domains (staleness), patterns, rules + lazy index
docs T4 product modules (RNs/PENDs, ADRs, TRACEABILITY, features, specs) — combinable with --scope <module>
all (default) T1-T5 everything (historical skill behavior)

Combinable with + (e.g. what: workflow+pack). Cross-store edges (indice_lazy T5→T3, fundado_em T5→T1, aplica_em T2→T4) only appear when BOTH source and destination stores are selected.

  • Parity: the gm-knowledge-graph 38-check fixture is the parity criterion — the Go command's graph.json and HTML are byte-identical to the reference Node extractor (except gerado_em, normalized; MINUTE precision for output idempotence), including per-type counts, warnings in the same order, and the HTML JSON embed. knowledge-graph.md diverges only in the provenance line ("Generated by golmet graph (kit deterministic engine — ADR-019)"); the fixture md baseline is frozen from Go itself.
  • Alternatives considered:
    • Hybrid MCP→node (tool spawns node build-knowledge-graph.mjs): REJECTED — contradicts the principle above (deterministic work lives in the CLI, not in an external runtime orchestrated by the MCP), keeps the Node ≥ 18 dependency (IMP-148) and the fragility of a materialized script path; the IMP-008 experience (a skill documenting a script that did not exist — ghost component) is the historical evidence that the runtime→script indirection is a silent single point of failure.
    • Keep the .mjs as reference and Go as mirror: two engines to maintain = guaranteed drift; the fixture with the frozen .mjs baseline already serves as the reference without duplicated code.
    • Fully agentic skill (no engine): manual parsing at scale by the runtime — forbidden by the skill's own error mode (R4/IMP-148) and the root cause of IMP-008.
  • Consequences:
    • ✓ Node ≥ 18 is no longer a requirement for THIS skill (IMP-148 remains valid for other consumers, if any)
    • ✓ 15th MCP tool (gm_graph) with the same trust contract as the others (structured JSON, declared degradation)
    • ✓ Byte-for-byte auditable determinism between CLI and MCP (same Go function)
    • ✓ The files: renderer infrastructure (previous cycle) remains as a generic capability for future skills with scripts
    • ✗ The .mjs is REMOVED in the same release — the parity baseline in the fixture is the record of the reference behavior
    • ✗ The port requires parity discipline on every engine evolution (the fixture eval is the gate)

This file is maintained by the GOLMET Quadri (gm-req, gm-doc, gm-dev, gm-devops) and updated when new architectural decisions are made. Each ADR is immutable after registration - revised decisions get a new entry referencing the previous one.
